name: Why Do Kitchen Remodels Go Over Budget?

mainEntity.name: What causes kitchen remodel projects in Los Angeles County to go over budget?
mainEntity.text: What causes kitchen remodel projects in Los Angeles County to go over budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kitchen remodels go over budget for a few repeatable reasons. The most common are hidden conditions discovered after demolition, homeowner changes during construction, allowance amounts that are too low, and bids that did not fully include permits, cleanup, or finish details. In Los Angeles County, material lead times and inspection timing can also create indirect costs if the schedule slips. The best way to reduce overruns is to lock the scope before demolition and make product selections early. Ask the contractor to identify every allowance and every likely excluded item. That includes fixtures, appliances, tile, flooring, paint, trim, disposal, and any structural or code-related corrections that may arise. A good contractor should also explain the change-order process in advance. If you know how additions are priced and approved, you can make decisions quickly instead of accumulating small overruns that snowball. Budget control depends less on luck and more on how clearly the job is defined before it starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common budget overruns come from change orders, hidden damage, material upgrades, permit delays, incomplete scope definitions, and selection changes after work starts. Underpriced allowances can also make a bid look cheaper than it really is. A detailed scope and contingency reduce surprises.
